summary: Managed browser automation: per-agent VM browser sessions, login profiles, owner hand-off and checks.

help:
Browser automation through st

Agent quick path: your own Chrome on the browser VM, off the owner's screen.
  st browser session create NAME            then put --session NAME on every command
  st browser --session NAME open URL
  st browser --session NAME observe         the page as text with @refs (narrow: --selector CSS;
                                            over 20000 characters it's cut, whole text to a file; --max-chars N)
  st browser --session NAME step click @e1 | step fill @e2 TEXT | step press Enter
  st browser --session NAME wait --load networkidle   (still loading? then observe again)
  st browser --session NAME back | scroll down | get url | get title | get text @e1 | screenshot [path]
  st browser --session NAME eval <js>
  st browser --session NAME tab new URL | tab list | tab t1 | tab close t2
  st browser session status NAME | list     idle time and auto-close, in words
  st browser session close NAME             when done; profile and logins kept, create reopens it
  st browser check <project-or-url> [png] [--viewports desktop,narrow,mobile]   screenshot check
  Without --session: your own default session. Keep one identity (ST_BROWSER_OWNER, else your agent
  id) throughout; subagents use a --session NAME each. Auto-close: idle 20 min, ended agent, paused
  2 h. Profiles kept 7 days unused (login profiles always). Listed at https://browser.summitflow.dev.
  Refs change when the page does: observe again after navigating. Help: <command> --help (session,
  observe, run, step, get, tab...), capabilities [topic].
  Exit codes: 1 the command failed (a page that would not open, a check with issues), 2 wrong usage or an action that did not complete, e.g. no_effect (a click, fill or select changed nothing: click --help) or no session, 4 declined, 69 unavailable (VM/desktop),
  75 busy (paused or in use: retry), 124 timed out.

Owner hand-off (login, 2FA, captcha): st browser session pause --reason "login needed: <site>" --wait
Owner's Chrome tabs, shared login profiles, workflows, targets, local rules and examples: st browser help all
help.login:
Usage: st browser [--session NAME | --selected-tab TAB_ID|HANDLE] login TARGET [--actor NAME]
       st browser login add TARGET [--actor NAME] --url LOGIN_URL
       st browser login list
       st browser login api TARGET PATH [--actor NAME] [--out FILE]

Logs back in to a site with the login the owner saved for TARGET (a bug bounty platform, say). It opens the
saved login page in your VM session (no --session: your own; a named one needs st browser session create NAME
first) or in a tab of the owner's AI profile, fills username,
password and authenticator code, submits, and says whether the login form is gone and where the page went.
No login form at the saved page is a failure (a site root or portal, not the login page). You never see the values.
Then look: st browser [same route] observe. Each field is typed once, so a wrong password is not retried.
The owner saves logins on Aico's Logins page, or with login add at a real terminal: it
asks for username, password and optional authenticator secret (base32 or otpauth:// URI); no terminal, no prompt.
login list names the saved logins this session may use (TARGET and actor; never values). A login you may
not use yet: aico logins allow TARGET gives you access yourself (logged, no owner step); a wrong login page:
aico logins edit TARGET --login-url URL. Only a wrong or missing username or password goes to the owner.
login api reads (GET) TARGET's API (its saved login URL's site) with its saved token and prints the JSON
answer, e.g. st browser login api hackerone-api /v1/hackers/me/reports. A long answer is saved whole to
./.dev-tools/ and summarised (items, next page), for jq; --out FILE saves any answer there instead. It never writes; HackerOne report drafts come from
st neri advance CASE ready.
Exit codes: 0 logged in; 3 login form or code prompt still showing (wrong or expired password, captcha, or no
authenticator secret saved), no login form at the saved page, or the login page went to another site (nothing
typed there): each message names the fix; 66 no usable login for TARGET; 69 browser not reachable; 2 other.
help.preview:
Usage: st browser preview <file-or-url> [--session NAME]

Show a local file or HTTP(S) URL on the owner's desktop and leave it open.
Creates/reuses your named local Chrome session; resumes closed sessions.
Verifies the page URL and raises its window. Paused or remote sessions stay protected.
Use the printed session for follow-up: st browser --local-ai --session NAME observe
Close when the owner is finished: st browser --local-ai session close NAME
Previews are never closed for idleness or an ended agent: they stay until the owner closes the window or you close the session; profiles are kept.

usage.when: UI render verification; screenshots; DOM snapshots; web tasks in a browser
precautions: each agent gets its own VM browser session; st browser session close when done
login, 2FA or captcha: st browser session pause --reason "login needed: <site>" --wait
logged-in accounts: --shared-profile NAME (e.g. linkedin), one agent at a time
use st ui when the open desktop/PWA is the right evidence source
never start arbitrary chrome/CDP on project or server host, nor set ST_BROWSER_HOST / ST_BROWSER_VM_ID without approval; local-AI profile and Dark Reader: st browser help all

usage.when: show the owner a local HTML/mockup; leave it open
precautions: reuse the printed session for follow-up; never use an unqualified observe
